title: California Car Registration After Moving
read: You're welcome — and if you do end up registering, you'll also need a **California driver's license within 10 days** of becoming a resident, which you can do at the same DMV appointment.
ok calling geico tomorrow. how much will the fees be roughly. 2019 civic

Rough estimate for a **2019 Honda Civic** being registered in CA for the first time:

| Fee | Approx. |
|---|---|
| Registration fee | ~$70 |
| CHP fee | ~$30 |
| Vehicle License Fee (0.65% of current value; ~$16k car) | ~$100 |
| Transportation Improvement Fee (by value) | ~$60–$100 |
| County/district fees (SF) | ~$20–$40 |
| New-resident title & smog fees | ~$30–$50 |
| Smog check at a station | ~$50–$70 |
| **Total** | **~$350–$450** |

No use tax if you've owned it more than 12 months before moving. Use the DMV's online fee calculator for the exact amount once you have the VIN.
im on a leave from grad school in virginia, not sure if im a resident yet. i might go back

That's a gray area. A few things that matter:

* **Students and temporary visitors:** nonresident students attending school in California can keep out-of-state registration. You're the reverse — a Virginia student temporarily in CA.
* **Employment:** if you're working in California (including running a company here), the DMV generally treats you as a resident for registration purposes, even if you plan to go back.
* **Intent and duration:** a short, defined stay (e.g., a 3-month internship) is different from an open-ended move.

What I'd do:
1. Call your **insurer** first. Many insurers require you to update the garaging address when you move; if you have a claim with the car garaged in SF on a Virginia policy, that can be a problem regardless of registration.
2. If your stay is open-ended and you're working here, plan to register. The 20-day window is already running.

I'm not a lawyer — the DMV's residency rules page is the authority here.
moved from virginia to san francisco aug 8. car is registered in VA. do i need to register in CA and how fast

Yes. California requires you to register your vehicle **within 20 days** of becoming a resident. Things that establish residency include taking a job, renting a place, or enrolling kids in school.

**Steps**
1. **Smog check** — required for most gasoline cars being registered in CA for the first time (exceptions for very new cars, electric vehicles, and some hybrids). Use a licensed smog station.
2. **Vehicle verification** — a DMV employee (or licensed verifier) physically checks the VIN. Often done at the DMV visit.
3. **Apply at the DMV** with:
   * Your **VA title** (or lienholder info if you have a loan),
   * VA registration,
   * Smog certificate,
   * Proof of **California insurance**,
   * Form **REG 343** (Application for Title or Registration).
4. **Pay fees** — includes registration fee, vehicle license fee (based on the car's value) and possibly a **use tax** if you bought the car within the last 12 months outside CA.

Make a DMV appointment online; SF offices book up fast.
